profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC16 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC16 is a 250,000 square foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia with N+2 cooling redundancy, but the operator has not published its power capacity. Without a megawatt figure, its size relative to other data centers cannot be determined from published sources. This facility is one of 16 buildings in Equinix's Washington DC metro region, which spans Ashburn, Manassas, and Culpeper County.

The Ashburn corridor is positioned as North America's largest peering point and a major gateway to Europe, making it strategically significant for network routing and international traffic. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power capacity figures. The 1,375 megawatts of published capacity across the state ranks 24th by facility among those with disclosed figures, though this aggregates diverse operators and facility types.

DC16's capacity is not measurable from available public data. To assess whether this facility matters to AI scaling, one would need to obtain the power capacity directly from Equinix or infer it from utilization disclosures, neither of which are in published specifications. Its position within a major metro hub suggests relevance to AI infrastructure planning in the region, but the absence of a published megawatt figure means its individual contribution cannot be quantified from operator-disclosed sources.
